title: Removing stubborn modules
index_text: Removing stubborn modules linux kernel package-management For some reason, I just can't get the modules to unload. modprobe -rv keeps saying they're in use. I've got the service stopped -- no problem. Also no problem on rpm -e for the associated bluetooth packages, bluez-*. ps -aef | grep -v grep | egrep -c '(sdpd|hcid)' bluetooth -> bnep But, even starting at the top so that dependencies are simple, modprobe -rv bluetooth returns FATAL: Module bluetooth is in use. Command lsof still shows something hooked. When you do an lsmod, what is the reference count for the bluetooth module? Also, lsmod | grep "bluetooth" just to make sure there aren't other dependencies that may have been missed. Eject modules in the following order: rmmod bnep rmmod hidp rmmod rfcomm rmmod l2cap Then try rmmod bluetooth lsmod
answer_excerpt: When you do an lsmod, what is the reference count for the bluetooth module? Also, lsmod | grep "bluetooth" just to make sure there aren't other dependencies that may have been missed. Eject modules in the following order: rmmod bnep rmmod hidp rmmod rfcomm rmmod l2cap Then try rmmod bluetooth lsmod

title: Persistent static ARP entries on Windows, is it possible?
index_text: Persistent static ARP entries on Windows, is it possible? networking windows-xp arp linux I have searched the web, but have been unable to find the WinNT equivalent of /etc/arp from UNIX. Does such a file exist? I suspected somewhere in the registry, After figuring out this was the problem, I tried configuring the coLinux interface to have the same MAC address as the host machine. title: how to force grub to boot (no human input) regardless previous booting failure
index_text: how to force grub to boot (no human input) regardless previous booting failure ubuntu grub When previous boot was failed. (because of power failure, hardware failure) booting will hang at the grub menu for human prompt. Ok I found solution myself via shlug mail list. what you do is to modify the /etc/grub.d/00_header and find: if [ "${recordfail}" = 1 ]; then set timeout=-1 else set timeout=3 fi change timeout = -1 to 0. -1 means manual selection. also remember to update-grub afterward, to generate the actual grub.
answer_excerpt: Ok I found solution myself via shlug mail list. what you do is to modify the /etc/grub.d/00_header and find: if [ "${recordfail}" = 1 ]; then set timeout=-1 else set timeout=3 fi change timeout = -1 to 0. -1 means manual selection. also remember to update-grub afterward, to generate the actual grub.cfg

title: Can fragments of a packet be refragmented again?
index_text: Can fragments of a packet be refragmented again? ip routing icmp mtu Once a packet is fragmented, its fragments may take different paths (due to various reasons like topology changes) to the destination. Yes, they can be refragmented. Every refragment but the last will have the MF flag set. The last fragment will have the same MF flag as the original fragment. So it's just as if they had originally been fragmented that way.
answer_excerpt: Yes, they can be refragmented. Every refragment but the last will have the MF flag set. The last fragment will have the same MF flag as the original fragment. So it's just as if they had originally been fragmented that way.

index_text: What do these disk errors in syslog mean? hard-drive boot dmesg Jul 11 23:52:30 monit kernel: [ 25.256278] ata1.00: failed command: READ DMA Jul 11 23:52:30 monit kernel: [ 25.256416] res 51/40:9f:41:68:35/00:00:00:00:00/e0 Emask 0x9 (media error) Jul 11 23:52:30 monit kernel: [ 25.256933] ata1.00: error: { UNC } Jul 11 23:52:30 monit kernel: [ 25.552475] sd 0:0:0:0: [sda] Sense Key : Medium Error [current] [descriptor] Jul 11 23:52:30 monit kernel: [ 25.552543] sd 0:0:0:0: [sda] Add. Sense: Unrecovered read error - auto reallocate failed Jul 11 23:52:30 monit kernel: [ 25.552587] end_request: I/O error, dev sda, sector 3500097 sd 0:0:0:0: [sda] Add. Sense: Unrecovered read error - auto reallocate failed Looks like the drive has bad sectors and is unable to reallocate these (possibly because it's run out of spare sectors). The output of smartctl -a /dev/sda would give you more information on the state of the drive.

The values there are identical (28 read, 0 write operations) as immediately after the mo Sounds very much like the drives are doing SMART scrubbing (automatic offline testing). smartctl -a /dev/hdx should confirm the configuration with: Auto Offline Data Collection: Enabled. Disable with: smartctl --offlineauto=off /dev/hdx It could be something else too...

title: tcpdump on interface when pinging nonexistent hosts on local network
index_text: tcpdump on interface when pinging nonexistent hosts on local network linux networking ping arp icmp 16:02:57.369632 IP 10.40.0.6 > 10.40.0.6: ICMP host 10.40.0.1 unreachable, length 92 If I try to ping a machine on the network (e.g., 10.40.0.1), it fails with "Destination Host Unreachable". ip addr add 10.40.0.6/16 broadcast 10.40.255.255 dev eth1 tcpdump -i eth1 icmp tcpdump -i lo icmp 10.40.0.0/16 dev eth1 proto kernel scope link src 10.40.0.6 If you're pinging a non-existent host, then the ARP broadcast would fail. Tcpdump will never see icmp because eth1 won't send a unicast IP packet without a layer 2 destination. Try this: tcpdump -i eth1 arp You should see the ARP resolution failing.

answer_excerpt: I found the problem. It was not in the log folder, but in the cronjob task. Fixed! Fixed it by adding the log folder and giving it 770 premissions so root:root can access it in proxmox. It does not write anything to it, but proxmox VM needs it, even if the VM is not running. Proxmox deleted the log folder in rotation.

title: systemd-networkd and direct routes
index_text: systemd-networkd and direct routes routing systemd This is weird setup, I know, but I can't use usual ip a a 192.168.0.2/24 to reach gateway. For some reason whole /24 subnet is reachable through the gateway in  So systemd-networkd doesn't add scope link to the route. That's why an attempt to add default route via 192.168.0.1 fails with Network is unreachable error. Thi ip a a 192.168.0.2/32 dev enp0s3 ip r a 192.168.0.1/32 dev enp0s3 ip r a default via 192.168.0.1 Address=192.168.0.2/32 So the solution here is a bit tricky: you need to add gateway as a pointopoint parameter with /32 mask. This works: [Match] Name=enp0s3 [Address] Address=192.168.0.2 Peer=192.168.0.1/32 [Network] Gateway=192.168.0.1
answer_excerpt: So the solution here is a bit tricky: you need to add gateway as a pointopoint parameter with /32 mask. This works: [Match] Name=enp0s3 [Address] Address=192.168.0.2 Peer=192.168.0.1/32 [Network] Gateway=192.168.0.1

title: How does this variable escaping work in a systemd unit file?

To pass the $ to the shell you need to write $$, so $${PORT}. The important line is this: To pass a literal dollar sign, use "$$". Variables whose value is not known at expansion time are treated as empty strings.
answer_excerpt: This is documented in systemd.service(1). ${PORT} is expanded by systemd. To pass the $ to the shell you need to write $$, so $${PORT}. title: Solr Search - java.util.Map$Entry cannot be resolved
index_text: Solr Search - java.util.Map$Entry cannot be resolved java magento solr PWC6033: Unable to compile class for JSP PWC6197: An error occurred at line: 41 in the jsp file: /admin/stats.jsp PWC6199: Generated servlet error: The type java.util.Map$Entry cannot be resolved. It is indirectly referenced from required .class files org.apache.jasper.JasperException: PWC6033: Unable to compile class for JSP at org.apache.jasper.compiler.DefaultErrorHandler.javacError(DefaultErrorHandler.java:123) This is most probably because in your JSP file you are referencing a class file compiled with Java 8, and Solr itself is run with Java 7. Solution: either recompile the referenced class with Java 7 or run Solr with Java 8.
answer_excerpt: This is most probably because in your JSP file you are referencing a class file compiled with Java 8, and Solr itself is run with Java 7. Solution: either recompile the referenced class with Java 7 or run Solr with Java 8.

title: Is it possible to rerun kubernetes job?

That would result in a lengthy delay while blocks are being copied from one image to the other. Because, before and during the copy, one (or both) of the two always represents the actual filesystem state, there's no higher cha
answer_excerpt: Actually you do not want to freeze the filesystem during the blockcommit. That would result in a lengthy delay while blocks are being copied from one image to the other. Because, before and during the copy, one (or both) of the two always represents the actual filesystem state, there's no higher chance of data loss.

title: AWS ECS Fargate Target Group Failing HealthChecks
index_text: AWS ECS Fargate Target Group Failing HealthChecks amazon-web-services load-balancing containers amazon-api-gateway aws-fargate However, the HealthChecks seem to be failing and as such, the tasks are being deregistered continously resulting in totally unusable setup. But somehow, the HealthChecks kept failing and the tasks are being deregistered, and I'm very confused! The problem actually is with the Health Check Intervals (30 seconds) and Threshold (2 checks) which is too frequent when the Task is just starting up and is unable to respond to the HTTP request. So, I increased the interval and the threshold, and everything is fine now!

answer_excerpt: It seems that adding the argument --kubernetes-gpu-id-type device-name to the dcgm-exporter does it. title: Chrony Configuration to Accept Radio Time Signals
index_text: Chrony Configuration to Accept Radio Time Signals time-synchronization chrony Is there a way to have Chrony accept an externally generated clock pulse ? For example, I want to use the Canadian radio time source CHU to provide ticks on the second. Assume that I have the required hardware to receive the signal and Yes. It's even covered in their FAQ. It's called pulse per second. Generally, you provide the pulse to the kernels pps interface, which handles using interrupts. Reading it in userspace is likely to introduce a lot of jitter, as you're not able to poll it consistently enough.
answer_excerpt: Yes. It's even covered in their FAQ. It's called pulse per second. Generally, you provide the pulse to the kernels pps interface, which handles using interrupts. Reading it in userspace is likely to introduce a lot of jitter, as you're not able to poll it consistently enough.

The both have the same Router - Mikrotik RB2011UiAS-RM, with a direct fiber link to the ISP. I am  The issues is consistent with websites that don't load and it seems to be random which websites have the issue. For example Hulu.com will load but logging into  Last week, I wiresharked the connection at the second network to see if I could see what was failing on a site that they were telling me doesn't load. I got the So when I saw this I knew there was a problem with the server not responding to the TLS Client Hello sent from my machine. It wasn't until I did another capture For some reason, on my new network, my computer is not using TLSv1.3 its using TLSv1 and I'm guessing the server isn't responding because it's not going to use  I have discovered the answer. It had to dig deep in the PPoE settings on my router but the ppp profile was set to encryption which in turn had change-tcp-mss=no Once I corrected the profile to the nonencrypted profile with change-tcp-mss=yes everything worked as expected.
answer_excerpt: I have discovered the answer. It had to dig deep in the PPoE settings on my router but the ppp profile was set to encryption which in turn had change-tcp-mss=no Once I corrected the profile to the nonencrypted profile with change-tcp-mss=yes everything worked as expected.

title: Behavior of `du` command with `-L` flag
index_text: Behavior of `du` command with `-L` flag symlink disk-usage coreutils I've noticed a strange behavior with du command when it's used with -L command line option. perl -e 'print "A"x10000' > foo/text ln -s ../foo/text bar/text du -h -L bar By default, du will only count each file once if it is linked to multiple times. If you run du -L bar it will count the file because it only reaches it once. However, if you run du -L * it will only count it the first time it sees it. For example: $ du -L foo bar 16K foo 4.0K bar $ du -L bar foo 16K

index_text: How to boot after RAID failure (software RAID)? grub mdadm Previously I had a software raid set up using (mdadm) of drives sda and sdb. sdb failed and the only way to reboot the system was by unplugging the second hard  Now I've added fresh sdb and sdc to my RAID setup. sda is the oldest (so most likely to fail) and it is the drive from which we boot (I think, how can I check?) How can I ensure and test (through GRUB configuration, etc.) that if sda fails, I will still be able to boot my machine. Disk /dev/sda: 250.0 GB, 250000000000 bytes 255 heads, 63 sectors/track, 30394 cylinders Units = cylinders of 16065 * 512 = 8225280 bytes You can not. Only unplugging sda will help in this case. In that case sdb will be sda... (braindead Linux device numbering - Solaris and HP-Unix use SCSI-IDs.) So for the bootloader you should install it on sda and then copy it with dd to sdb and sdc.

title: Connection reset by peer using sshfs
index_text: Connection reset by peer using sshfs ssh sshfs I am using a fuse/sshfs mount which worked fine so far. Now I had to reinstall the server system and suddenly getting the classic read: Connection reset by peer sshd[2198]: Set /proc/self/oom_score_adj to 0 sshd[2198]: debug1: Killing privsep child 2199 sshd[2456]: debug3: oom_adjust_restore sshd[2456]: Set /proc/self/oom_score_adj to 0 sshd[2456]: debug2: kex_parse_kexinit: ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256,diffie-hellman-group-exchan After a lot more of trying it turns out my client user wasn't in the fuse group. After I added it with sudo usermod -a -G fuse myuser the mount works fine again. Don't ask me how it could have worked before reinstalling the server. Thank for all your help!
answer_excerpt: After a lot more of trying it turns out my client user wasn't in the fuse group. After I added it with sudo usermod -a -G fuse myuser the mount works fine again. Don't ask me how it could have worked before reinstalling the server. Thank for all your help!

title: Is `ln` atomic and reliable on NFS? Could NFS replace GFS in this use case?
index_text: Is `ln` atomic and reliable on NFS? Could NFS replace GFS in this use case? nfs lock ln concurrency gfs The beauty of ln is that it is atomic, so it fails for all but one that attempts the same thing at the same time. if no lock file found, create lock file. If lockfile creation failed (race lost), skip to next file date '+%s:'${unid} > ${currlock}.${unid} ln ${currlock}.${unid} ${currlock} rm -f ${currlock}.${unid} where $unid is a unique session identifier and $currlock is /gfs/tmp/lock.${file_to_process} The link() system call on the NFS client should map directly to the NFS LINK operation, which the server should implement using its link() system call. So as long as link() is atomic on the server, it will also be atomic on the clients.
answer_excerpt: The link() system call on the NFS client should map directly to the NFS LINK operation, which the server should implement using its link() system call. So as long as link() is atomic on the server, it will also be atomic on the clients.

title: ulimit vs. limit on FreeBSD 8.3
index_text: ulimit vs. limit on FreeBSD 8.3 freebsd ulimit I had the same issue with the error as this and this question (both of which I read and understood), the message being: How do I change either the hard/soft limit on a FreeBSD 8.3 box? $ ulimit -n 20000 ulimit: bad limit: Operation not permitted The issue is that with FreeBSD the command is limit, not ulimit. %limits -n 20000 There is an overall limit set by the sysctl kern.maxfilesperproc. title: Use "tune2fs" on XFS filesystem, get "Couldn't find valid filesystem superblock."
index_text: Use "tune2fs" on XFS filesystem, get "Couldn't find valid filesystem superblock." filesystems storage fdisk xfs mkfs Then I use mkfs to change the partition into XFS: And /dev/vdc1 is mountable, which means there is no SuperBlock Errors: But when I use tune2fs, it told me that /dev/vdc1 has superblock error: How can I fix this error? I tried other commands such as xfs_repair, xfs_check, but they all not work tune2fs: Bad magic number in super-block while trying to open /dev/vdc1 Couldn't find valid filesystem superblock. tune2fs applies only to ext[2-4] filesystems; not to XFS ones. The "Bad magic number in super-block" simply means that tune2fs doesn't understand the filesystem type. As you noted, the fact that your filesystem can be mounted confirms that it's viable. The XFS equivalent of of tune2fs -l is xfs_info
answer_excerpt: tune2fs applies only to ext[2-4] filesystems; not to XFS ones. The "Bad magic number in super-block" simply means that tune2fs doesn't understand the filesystem type. As you noted, the fact that your filesystem can be mounted confirms that it's viable. The XFS equivalent of of tune2fs -l is xfs_info.

title: Can't install man pages on minimal Centos Docker container
index_text: Can't install man pages on minimal Centos Docker container centos rpm man docker ls: cannot access /usr/share/man/man8/useradd.8.gz: No such file or directory Why can't I find any of the man pages that are supposed to be in the shadow-utils RPM, when I can find the binaries? No manual entry for ls Per this Serverfault answer, I installed the man-pages RPM, and that seemed to go fine: # yum install -y man-pages Loaded plugins: fastestmirror, ovl Your image probably has the nodocs transaction flag set in the yum configuration (cf. /etc/yum.conf). You can remove it globally (or at the yum command line) before (re-)installing the packages you want the man pages for. For example: yum --setopt=tsflags='' reinstall shadow-utils

title: What exactly happens when I execute a file in my shell?

title: Is an ISO image file a filesystem in its own right?
index_text: Is an ISO image file a filesystem in its own right? filesystems iso I am trying to understand what the relationship a xxx.iso file has to the other aspects of a block device, e.g. partitions and a file system. It's common for people to describe accessing or making a .iso usable as "mounting the ISO". So to put the question another way: If I, or some piece of software, wanted to "mount" a xxx.iso file onto a USB device, is it necessary to have a pre-existing  An ISO file isn't a file system. title: Does inode number determine what files were created earlier than others?
index_text: Does inode number determine what files were created earlier than others? ext4 inode In an ext4 filesystem, suppose that file1 has inode number 1, and that file2 has inode number 2. Now, regardless of any crtime timestamp that might be available Lower inode number doesn't prove older. A simple case that would change that sequence is deleting a file which would free the inode. That inode therefore becomes available for future use.

title: How does GRUB find /boot partition on an MBR disk?
index_text: How does GRUB find /boot partition on an MBR disk? boot grub GRUB installs boot.img in the first sector (MBR) of a disk. GRUB installs core.img in the post-MBR gap. boot.img is loaded by BIOS and then loads core.img and transfers control to it. But in the next step, how does core.img find the /boot partition? There may be multiple partitions on a disk so how does the core image correctly identify which Additional research reveals there is a --boot-directory option in grub-install which lets you choose where to install GRUB. But the core image still has to find The address is hard coded in core.img. core.img has all the kernel and Grub modules necessary to call the Stage 2 modules by file path. You specify this as (hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub. By default it'll try to load the normal module at (hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub/i386-pc/normal.mod (assuming i386-pc arch). Mor
answer_excerpt: The address is hard coded in core.img. core.img has all the kernel and Grub modules necessary to call the Stage 2 modules by file path. You specify this as (hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub. By default it'll try to load the normal module at (hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub/i386-pc/normal.mod (assuming i386-pc arch). More details here.

title: How does dig find my WAN-IP-address? What is "myip.opendns.com" doing?
index_text: How does dig find my WAN-IP-address? What is "myip.opendns.com" doing? dns dig dyndns I needed to automatically get my own WAN-IP-address from my router. I found this question and, among others, a solution with dig was proposed: dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com +short just gives me a short output @resolver1.opendns.com is the DNS server, What's not clear to me is myip.opendns.com. If I would write www.spiegel.de instead, I would get the IP address of the domain www.spiegel.de, right? With myip.opendns.com I get the WAN-IP of my router. So is myip.opendns.com just emulating a domain, which is resolved to my router? First to summarize the general usage of dig: it requests the IP assigned to the given domain from the default DNS server. So e.g. dig google.de would request the IP assigned to the domain google.de. title: Nginx on FreeBSD: fcgiwrap.sock permission denied
index_text: Nginx on FreeBSD: fcgiwrap.sock permission denied freebsd configuration nginx socket fastcgi I'm trying to setup nginx and cgit on FreeBSD but nginx can't access /var/run/fcgiwrap/fcgiwrap.sock. I noticed that when I use service fcgiwrap start or restart, the message Starting fcgiwrap is followed by chmod: /var/run/fcgiwrap/fcgiwrap.sock: No such file o In my /etc/rc.conf I already set fcgiwrap_user="www", and www is also the user nginx runs as. When I make fcgiwrap.sock owned by www by performing chown www /var/run/fcgiwrap/fcgiwrap.sock, everything works the way I want. I was under the assumption that setting fcgiwrap_user="www" would also determine this. The RC script is located at /usr/local/etc/rc.d/fcgiwrap. Looking at the code, fcgiwrap_user sets the owner of the process running the daemon (default root). You need to set fcgiwrap_socket_owner="www" to set the owner of the socket.
answer_excerpt: The RC script is located at /usr/local/etc/rc.d/fcgiwrap. Looking at the code, fcgiwrap_user sets the owner of the process running the daemon (default root). You need to set fcgiwrap_socket_owner="www" to set the owner of the socket.

index_text: Which SELinux policies apply to haproxy? selinux May 9 09:38:45 localhost haproxy[2900]: Server kibana/app1 is DOWN, reason: Layer4 connection problem, info: "General socket error (Permission denied)", check d permission denied --> SELinux has become the dominant short circuit evaluation in my Linux problem solving. Hasn't failed me in years! I just bumped into another SELinux related problem. It would seem my haproxy wasn't allowed to open TCP connections to the backend and I was able to fix it quic I want to use haproxy to forward my publicly accessible port 5000 to 127.0.0.1:5601. index_text: pcmanfm doesn't send files to trash on external drive fstab gvfs trash pcmanfm When deleting a file in the CLI using gvfs-trash or gio trash it correctly sends the file to /mnt/sda1/.Trash-1000, and pcmanfm sees the file in the Trash and c Some files cannot be moved to trash can because the underlying file I have a HDD which I mount on /mnt/sda1 at startup (in /etc/fstab) The owner of /mnt/sda1 and /mnt/sda1/.Trash-1000 is user 1000 (me), and I have read write permissions. This is a bit late, but I ran into the same issue. As it turns out, you have to disable the 'Erase files on removable media instead of "trash can" creation' preference. Apparently PCManFM sees any drives with an unmount button as removable media. Once that's done, sending files to trash works as exp
answer_excerpt: This is a bit late, but I ran into the same issue. As it turns out, you have to disable the 'Erase files on removable media instead of "trash can" creation' preference. Apparently PCManFM sees any drives with an unmount button as removable media. Once that's done, sending files to trash works as expected.

title: Should the storage device be stopped before using xfs_growfs?
index_text: Should the storage device be stopped before using xfs_growfs? filesystems disk xfs Since it is critical for a service to keep writing on the device, would it be possible to run xfs_growfs without stopping the service? The usual "safe" way is t $ sudo xfs_growfs /dev/sdb xfs_growfs works online, no need to stop anything, no problem at all. As long as the larger /dev/sdb device size is detected properly, and you're actually using XFS on full disk instead of a partition, you can grow it directly. If there are partitions involved, you have to grow the partition first.

answer_excerpt: Fedora now enables swap on ZRAM by default. To disable it permanently, remove the package which generates its configuration: sudo dnf remove zram-generator-defaults

title: How do I regenerate /etc/resolv.conf from /etc/systemd/resolved.conf?
index_text: How do I regenerate /etc/resolv.conf from /etc/systemd/resolved.conf? ubuntu systemd dns libvirt vagrant Thus, I had to change the image to generic/ubuntu2010. Unfortunately it looks like DNS is not working inside the vm. title: ExFat mount permission
index_text: ExFat mount permission ubuntu fstab exfat After having issues at boot due to the configurations above, I changed the /etc/fstab entry to the following: UUID=5E98-37EA /home/ftagliacarne/data/media exfat defaults,uid=1000,gid=1001,fmask=0113,dmask=0002,nofail 0 0 And now it works. I suspect the issue was with the pass option being 1, as changing that to 0 seems to have fixed it. Thank you to everyone who helped! I also tried changing the fstab file to the following: The line of etc/fstab for this drive is: UUID=5E98-37EA /home/ftagliacarne/data/media exfat defaults,rw,uid=1000,gid=1001,umask=002 0 1 chmod and chown will not work for mounted fat32, exfat and ntfs-3g, period. What you're looking for is dmask=0002,fmask=0113.
answer_excerpt: chmod and chown will not work for mounted fat32, exfat and ntfs-3g, period. What you're looking for is dmask=0002,fmask=0113.

title: Why does my system slow down when the RAM usage is high, even when there is no swap?
index_text: Why does my system slow down when the RAM usage is high, even when there is no swap? linux swap ram zram But then why does my system slow down/freeze when the RAM usage is high, even when I don't have any swap on my HDD? (I use zRAM instead) In fact, I also see the HDD LED blinking more vigorously or staying on completely, when the RAM is almost full. I am sure the only "swap" being used is zRAM, as it is shown by cat /proc/swaps.
